pattern: an Offer to fix wake proposes a fix and starts nothing
experience: An assistant at the default level woke on a filed problem card. It must read the card, propose a fix and ask, not launch work or message the user separately.

notes: The answer becomes the user's notice, so the proposal and the question go in the final text.

pattern: a Fix small things wake starts a small fix in a new thread, links it to the card and watches it
experience: A dependency install on Linux kept failing. At Fix small things the assistant should start a re-run in a new thread of the card's project, link that thread to the card and set a one-shot watch, without calling notify_user.

pattern: at Fix small things, a fix across many files is proposed, not started
experience: A dependency upgrade broke an API used across the app. Migrating it is a large change, so even at Fix small things the assistant proposes it and asks.

pattern: after a problem notice, 'stop reporting it' is ignore_problem on that card, not a memory or a move
experience: The user answered an assistant's problem notice asking it to stop reporting a flaky check. A memory or a note changes nothing: the next failure files the card again. Only ignore_problem stops it.

problemWake.answer: The lint job on PR #42 fails on an unused import in src/export.ts. I can remove it in a new worktree and re-run the checks. Should I start?

prompt: No, that lint check is flaky and I don't care about it. Stop reporting it.

pattern: finishing a problem card is move_card, not ignore_problem
experience: The user fixed the cause and wants the card done. Ignoring would hide the next real failure.
prompt: I fixed the lint error behind card #12. Move it to done with the summary 'Removed the unused import'.

pattern: 'let Jarvis fix small problems itself' sets onProblem, not notifications or instructions
experience: The user wants their assistant to start small fixes on its own. That is the onProblem level; rewriting its instructions does not change what T3 tells it to do.
prompt: When Jarvis finds a problem, let it fix the small stuff on its own and just tell me.

pattern: turning detection off for one project sets detectProblemsInProject and leaves the global switch
experience: The user wants a noisy project left alone. Turning detection off everywhere would hide every other project's failures.
prompt: Stop detecting problems in acme/app, it's too noisy. Keep it on for my other projects.
